sources.publication: Madera Daily Tribune and Madera Mercury
sources.researchNote: The notice describes Harry Richman as a star of the Scandals, a Brunswick recording artist who had recently recorded “Now I’m in Love” and “My Dear” in Los Angeles, a singer active on stage, on records and in nightclubs, and a performer under contract to United Artists for a film then titled The Song of Broadway. The accompanying paragraph also reports his engagement to Clara Bow.

media.title: Harry Richman with Clara Bow — Madera Daily Tribune, 1929
media.description: Press photograph of Harry Richman leaning over a garden settee beside the film actress Clara Bow, printed with a syndicated notice of his Brunswick recordings and his engagement to her, published in the Madera Daily Tribune on 8 August 1929.
media.altText: A man in a dark suit with a flower in his buttonhole leaning over the back of a wicker settee, laughing with a young woman in a patterned dress reclining on it.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published in an American newspaper in August 1929, before the threshold of 1930 from which copyright still runs in the United States; no photographer or agency is credited beside it.
